member.name: M:Graphs.BandwidthEstimation.LogScaleBandwidth(System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Double},System.Span{System.Double},System.Double)
member.summary: Bandwidth derived from MAD on log-distances, back-transformed to distance units. For hyperbolic metrics whose NN distance distribution is roughly log-normal (volume of a hyperbolic ball grows exponentially with radius, so distances compress near the origin and stretch near the boundary).
member.remarks: Formula: logD[i] = log(d[i] + 1) (the +1 stabilises near-zero distances); compute med = median(logD) and mad = mad(logD); bandwidth = exp(med + mad·kernelFactor) − 1. The +1/−1 pair is symmetric and undoes itself; the median offset anchors the bandwidth at the typical distance scale rather than at zero.

member.name: T:Graphs.GraphBuildResult
member.summary: Rich-shape return for and . Carries the assembled plus the intermediate artifacts that downstream diagnostics need: the directed (pre-symmetrization) , the resolved bandwidth, and the nearest-neighbor distance sample that bandwidth was derived from.

remarks.para: Why this exists. The bare CsrGraph return loses information that diagnostics need — Hubness.Analyze wants the directed selection (counting in-degree pre-symmetrization), NeighborhoodScale wants raw NN distances, and a bandwidth retroactive check wants to know what bandwidth was actually used. The historical Build path discarded all of this and forced consumers to re-run KNN to recover it.

Bandwidth discriminator. Exactly one of and is non-null: single-kernel paths populate the former, mixture paths populate the latter. Consumers that need a representative scale without caring which side of the union it came from can read .

Metric provenance. is non-null when the caller supplied a custom — it carries the metric's name, bounded/domain properties, and the bandwidth strategy that was selected. Null when the inline default Euclidean path was used. Graph-health persistence records this so a reviewer can confirm "Poincaré → LogScaleHyperbolic" without re-reading the manifest's metric spec string.

member.name: M:Graphs.Proximity.ProximityGraph.SelectEpsilonBall(System.Int32,System.Double,System.Func{System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Double})
member.summary:
Epsilon-ball proximity. Edge (i,j) exists if d(i,j) < epsilon. Inherently symmetric given a symmetric distance function. K parameter is not used — all pairs within radius are included. Produces a variable-degree graph: dense regions get more edges, sparse regions get fewer. Can fail in high dimensions where distance concentration makes epsilon selection fragile.
Returns per-node neighbor lists and 1-NN distances for auto-delta.

member.name: M:Graphs.Proximity.ProximityGraph.SelectKnn(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Func{System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Double})
member.summary: Standard KNN proximity with OR-symmetrization. For each node, selects K nearest neighbors by raw distance. Then applies the OR rule: edge (i,j) exists if i is in j's KNN OR j is in i's KNN. Produces an undirected neighbor set where some nodes may have more than K neighbors after symmetrization.

member.name: M:Graphs.Proximity.ProximityGraph.SelectMutualKnn(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Func{System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Double})
member.summary: Mutual KNN proximity (AND-rule). Edge (i,j) exists only if i is in j's K-nearest AND j is in i's K-nearest. Produces a sparser graph than OR-symmetrized KNN with higher-confidence edges, but risks connectivity loss in high dimensions.

member.name: M:Graphs.Proximity.ProximityGraph.EnsureConnected(Graphs.NeighborSelection,System.Int32,System.Func{System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Double})
member.summary: Adds the minimum set of MST bridging edges needed to connect all components in . Works with any proximity rule (Knn, MutualKnn, EpsilonBall). Uses Borůvka phases: each phase is one O(N²) sweep finding the cheapest outgoing edge per component. Typical MutualKnn graphs (1–3 disconnected components) finish in 1–2 phases. Exits immediately if the graph is already connected. Returns a new NeighborSelection; the original is not modified.
